title: Facial Nerve Paresis and Paralysis

content_blocks.text: Dysfunction of the facial nerve (cranial nerve [CN] VII) causing paresis (weakness) or paralysis of the muscles of facial expression, which include the ears, eyelids, lips, and nostrils.
Central—impairment of the facial nucleus within the rostral medulla (brainstem).
Peripheral—impairment of the facial nerve anywhere along its length or at the neuromuscular junction.
Nervous—facial nerve peripherally or its nucleus centrally.

Ophthalmic—if parasympathetic preganglionic neurons that supply the lacrimal gland and gland of the third eyelid that course with the facial nerve proximally are affected, keratoconjunctivitis sicca (KCS) develops due to lack of tear secretion.
More common in dogs than cats.
